rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXLVII If Dignity or Honour shall continue
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: A new numbered chapter on duration of dignity begins lower original frame 656.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If the Dignity or Honour shall continue
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: This chapter asks whether already alleged honours persist, not their extent or cause.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planets who are in [glyph] with the Lights
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Source selects planets connected with the luminaries; first glyph/type uncertain.
Tight aspects to luminaries are another eligible method, not any remote planet.
When multiple eligible planets appear, the strongest is emphasized, without complete weights.
Jupiter as chosen light-contact planet provides a favorable source branch.
Venus provides another favorable source branch, not necessarily both planets required.
The positive duration conclusion explicitly requires strength, not simply benefic identity.
Lilly alleges continued rise, more than mere preservation of status.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: come and continue with ease and little labour
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: The author also alleges ease and minimal work, a separate subjective effort variable.
Benefics weakened moderately form a distinct middle condition.
Moderate benefics allegedly produce gradual rather than immediate improvement.
Even moderate positive testimony allegedly includes obstacles during status maintenance.
Weak benefic candidates form a third separate tier.
The source says weak benefic status lasts temporarily, not perpetually.
Temporary honor may decline but leave residual reputation; not absolute loss.
Saturn is not uniformly negative; strong/high-placed Saturn can indicate continuing dignity.
Mars provides a separate signifier alternative for the honor-continuation case.
The beneficial outcome from malefics requires favorable astronomical positioning.
Strong favorable malefic configurations allegedly preserve rank.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: many times in danger oft interruption
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Continuity under malefics still allegedly faces threats/interruption, separate from permanent loss.
Moderate accidental/essential strength alters the same malefic case.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Honour and Fame weares away by little
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Moderate malefics allegedly cause gradual erosion rather than sudden collapse.
Source preserves a residual honor category even after significant decline.
Extremely adverse placements form strongest loss condition.
The source predicts rapid complete disappearance under very weak/adverse malefics.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: When Mercury signification and aspects Luminaries
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Mercury must be selected and aspect lights, rather than Mercury anywhere in chart.
Mercurial light contacts allegedly indicate rapid initial status increases.
Initial prominence is said to persist for a limited but unquantified time.
The author claims maintenance difficulty for a strong Mercurial signal.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: for Mercury is an unstable Planet
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Lilly's interpretive rationale comes from a traditional character assigned to Mercury.
A mid-strength Mercury case is explicitly distinct from weak Mercury.
Moderate Mercury allegedly raises risk of lost honors, not necessarily actual loss.
The author says intellect might avert full loss, a practical countercondition not a chart-only rule.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: when unhappily posited nothing well dignified
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Weak/damaged Mercury forms a different source branch.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Honours encrease then end much unluckinesse
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: The adverse Mercurial case allows early success but severe subsequent loss.
Absence of planets aspecting luminaries is a required trigger for a fallback source.
The first fallback uses the planets occupying the tenth/Midheaven.
Planet's historical intrinsic classification determines possible persistence.
Planetary strength must be checked for the fallback rather than default success.
Essential dignity is separately specified as a test in the tenth-occupant fallback.
A second fallback applies only if the tenth has no planets.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: then judge from Lord of tenth
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: The tenth ruler is used only after the first fallback fails.
Fixed sign placement of tenth ruler is a criterion for duration.
The tenth-house sign/cusp must also be fixed, distinct from ruler's sign.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if Sun friendlier aspect cusp or lord
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Sun supportive aspect is one alternative source of continuity.
Moon beneficial contact provides an alternative support condition.
Jupiter adds a separate benefic continuation source.
Venus adds another allowed source support factor.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: aspect cusp tenth or Lord thereof
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: The source specifies the benefit may go to either tenth cusp or tenth ruler.
Combined fixed-sign and friendly-aspect testimony allegedly predicts continuation, not size.
Unnumbered internal aphorisms are part of printed CXLVII rather than a new numbered chapter.
Stellar placements at angles are a source precondition for status rise/reversal.
Hyades is one named star cluster in the source fixed-star list.
Hercules appears separately in same original fixed-star list.
Scorpion heart star appears as another high-impact stellar condition.
Lanx Australis (southern scale) completes list across original frame boundary.
Adverse square/opposition to stars is a qualifying source for eventual reversal.
The source alleges unusually large ascent from poverty to prominence.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: cast down at last with vengeance
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: The same strong stellar source may later cause dramatic collapse, not guaranteed durable success.
The next aphorism's exact Sun sign glyphs remain unresolved; no executable status rule.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun with good/ill Planets or fixed starres
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Planet or fixed-star company adds further clauses to next reversal case.
An unfavorable primary direction is one required time trigger.
Another unfavorable revolution event is required for catastrophic fall.
The compounded ill-direction/revolution case allegedly causes prolonged loss.
Only one adverse trigger is an explicit alternative case.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: cast down present but again rise
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: One-trigger variant alleges temporary fall followed by recovery.
A source political-moral judgment about rulers appears, separate from rank and duration.
The King/people joint-nativity criterion would require two independent charts, not one natal horoscope.
A lunar MC source for alleged infamy includes a sign requiring original glyph check.
Source adds a fourth-house malefic condition to alleged public infamy.
Author alleges a stigmatizing public reputation result, unsupported by measured population outcomes.
Separate source infamy claim has Moon in Scorpio.
The paired Mars Taurus condition is part of final source's compound case.
The final case alleges lifelong infamy, an unvalidated high-stakes moral classification.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXLVIII Of Magistery Exercitation or Profession
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Following original printed CXLVIII starts after divider in PDF658, separate from honor duration.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Astrologers name Magistery of Native a Study or Delight
rules.historical_source_meaning_only: Only next source opening definition retained as boundary witness, not counted as CXLVII rule.
